facts.raw_span: Temperature of 101.5°F
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
Normocytic anemia (mean corpuscular volume: 99 fL; hemoglobin: 11.7 g/dL; hematocrit: 33.4%)
Platelet count: 81 K/μL (thrombocytopenia)
Complement levels: C3 of 42 mg/dL; C4 of 3 mg/dL (hypocomplementemia)
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:1280 (speckled pattern)
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
Negative hepatitis panel

concepts.why: The patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and presents with fever, erythematous plaques, and a high antinuclear antibody titer, which are all consistent with an active lupus flare.
The patient has a history of photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and presents with erythematous plaques and atypical target lesions, which are characteristic of ACLE.

The patient presents with erythematous plaques and atypical target lesions, which are consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, a subtype of lupus that is characterized by skin lesions and positive anti-Ro antibodies.
The patient presents with bullae and atypical target lesions, which are consistent with bullous systemic lupus erythematosus, a rare subtype of lupus that is characterized by blistering skin lesions.
The patient presents with erythematous plaques and atypical target lesions, which are consistent with vasculitis, an inflammatory condition that can be associated with lupus.
The patient has a low platelet count, which is consistent with thrombocytopenia, a condition that can be associated with lupus.
The patient has a low red blood cell count, which is consistent with anemia, a condition that can be associated with lupus.
The patient has low complement levels, which is consistent with hypocomplementemia, a condition that can be associated with lupus.
